module.purpose: Provides TypeScript property-validation types and converts record property migration definitions into store-compatible migration sequences.
module.summary: This module defines type-level mappings between record properties and validators, describes property migration contracts, and adapts both current and legacy migration configurations for the store system. It creates empty retroactive sequences when no migrations exist, validates sequence identifiers for already-formed migrations, wraps property migrations with record-type filters, and translates legacy versioned migrators into ordered migration objects.
module.businessContext: Supports schema evolution for tldraw records such as shapes and bindings. Failure can prevent records from loading or migrating correctly across application versions.
functions: processPropsMigrations (~L155-221): Converts record migration configurations into store migration sequences.
createPropsMigration (~L247-271): Wraps a property migration as a filtered store migration.

mutationOfArg: Wrapped migrations mutate the input record's props when an up or down transformation returns a truthy result.

typeShapes.name: TLPropsMigration
typeShapes.shape:
{
	readonly id: MigrationId
	readonly dependsOn?: MigrationId[]
	// eslint-disable-next-line tldraw/method-signature-style
	readonly up: (props: any) => any
	/**
	 * If a down migration was deployed more than a couple of months ago it should be safe to retire it.
	 * We only really need them to smooth over the transition between versions, and some folks do keep
	 * browser tabs open for months without refreshing, but at a certain point that kind of behavior is
	 * on them. Plus anyway recently chrome has started to actually kill tabs that are open for too long
	 * rather than just suspending them, so if other browsers follow suit maybe it's less of a concern.
	 *
	 * @public
	 */
	readonly down?: 'none' | 'retired' | ((props: any) => any)
}

import {
	Migration,
	MigrationId,
	MigrationSequence,
	RecordType,
	StandaloneDependsOn,
	UnknownRecord,
	createMigrationSequence,
} from '@tldraw/store'
import { MakeUndefinedOptional, assert } from '@tldraw/utils'
import { T } from '@tldraw/validate'
import { SchemaPropsInfo } from './createTLSchema'

detail.name: processPropsMigrations
detail.signature: export function processPropsMigrations<R extends UnknownRecord & { type: string; props: object }>(typeName: R['typeName'], records: Record<string, SchemaPropsInfo>)
genericTypeParams: R extends UnknownRecord & { type: string; props: object }
preconditions: typeName identifies the record type being processed.
records is an object whose values conform to SchemaPropsInfo.
If a migrations definition contains sequenceId, it must equal com.tldraw.${typeName}.${subType} for its record subtype.
postconditions: Returns one MigrationSequence for each entry in records, in Object.entries(records) iteration order.
Every returned sequence has sequenceId com.tldraw.${typeName}.${subType} for its corresponding subtype.
Entries without migrations produce an empty retroactive migration sequence.
Sequence-based migrations are retroactive and preserve non-property migrations while converting entries containing an id through createPropsMigration.
Legacy migrators are converted into migrations ordered by ascending numeric version.
invariants: The generated sequence ID is derived from typeName and the records entry subtype.
Legacy migration IDs use the generated sequence ID followed by /${version}.
Generated migrations target only records whose typeName equals typeName and whose type equals the corresponding subtype.
Legacy migrator up and down results are returned only when the underlying migrator returns a truthy result.
edgeCases: An entry with no migrations produces a sequence with retroactive true and an empty sequence.
An entry with a sequenceId matching the generated ID is returned as the supplied migration sequence.
An entry with a mismatching sequenceId fails the assertion instead of being returned.
A sequence definition containing no migrations with id is wrapped without property-migration conversion.
Legacy migrator keys are converted to numbers and sorted numerically, so versions are processed in ascending order regardless of object-key order.
A legacy migrator up or down operation returning a falsy value yields no migration result for that operation.

raises: AssertionError from assert when a supplied migrations.sequenceId does not match the generated sequence ID
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Throws when a migrations definition containing sequenceId has a mismatched sequence ID.

detail.summary: Converts property migration definitions for each record subtype into migration sequences. It preserves validated migration sequences, wraps sequence definitions, supplies empty retroactive sequences when absent, and converts legacy migrators into ordered migrations.

specLiterals.role: Template for the migration sequence identifier generated for each subtype.

specLiterals.value: sequenceId mismatch for ${subType} ${RecordType} migrations. Expected '${sequenceId}', got '${migrations.sequenceId}'
specLiterals.role: Assertion message for a supplied sequence ID that does not match the generated identifier.
Scope assigned to generated legacy migrations.

specTests.then: The result contains one retroactive migration sequence with sequenceId 'com.tldraw.shape.geo' and an empty sequence.
The result contains a retroactive sequence with sequenceId 'com.tldraw.shape.geo', and each entry containing an id is converted through createPropsMigration while other entries are preserved.
The generated sequence orders migrations as versions 2 then 10, with IDs 'com.tldraw.shape.geo/2' and 'com.tldraw.shape.geo/10'.

detail.name: createPropsMigration
detail.signature: export function createPropsMigration<R extends UnknownRecord & { type: string; props: object }>(typeName: R['typeName'], subType: R['type'], m: TLPropsMigration): Migration
genericTypeParams: R extends UnknownRecord & { type: string; props: object }
preconditions: The supplied migration object provides an id and property migration callback m.up.
Records passed to the generated migration callbacks have a typeName and props value, and matching records have the specified subtype.
postconditions: The returned migration has the same id and dependsOn values as m.
The filter matches only records whose typeName equals typeName and whose type equals subType.
The up callback replaces record.props with the result of m.up when that result is truthy; otherwise record.props is unchanged.
If m.down is a function, the down callback replaces record.props with the result of m.down when that result is truthy; otherwise record.props is unchanged.
If m.down is not a function, the returned migration has no down callback.
invariants: The generated filter requires both the record type name and subtype to match.
Falsy results from property migration callbacks do not replace record.props.
Exceptions thrown by migration callbacks are not transformed by this function.
edgeCases: A record with a matching typeName but a different subtype is rejected by filter.
A record with a matching subtype but a different typeName is rejected by filter.
When m.up returns a falsy value, the up callback leaves record.props unchanged.
When m.down is absent or not a function, no down callback is provided.
When m.down returns a falsy value, the down callback leaves record.props unchanged.

raises: Exceptions thrown by m.up or m.down propagate to the caller.

stateMutations: Mutates record.props in the generated up callback when m.up returns a truthy result.
Mutates record.props in the generated down callback when m.down returns a truthy result.
detail.summary: Creates a record-scoped migration that applies a property migration only to records matching the specified record type name and subtype. It preserves the migration identity and dependency metadata and conditionally updates record properties from the migration callbacks.

specLiterals.role: The migration scope assigned to the returned Migration.

specTests.then: The returned migration has id 'm1', dependsOn ['m0'], scope 'record', the filter returns true, and its up callback replaces record.props with { value: 2 }.
